Messages.Author: The Corrupter
Messages.Body:
(Steve) mag...@umdsun2.umd.umich.edu wrote:

> I have to agree Misdirection becomes way too powerful.

And unfortunately, you don't answer this anywhere below...

> And of course
> there is some thought to when to play them... (BTW: We play it's a
> Thaumaturgy card, not clan specific)

As a Thaumaturgy card, my disagreements would increase, this would change
the power dynamic between disciplines on top of everything else. The
only reason I didn't disagree about the card screwing up clan dynamic
(other than the simple untap fact) is that it is difficult to gauge by
mere numbers how many each _ought_ to have.

> You havbe to remmeber though,
> it'st's a Universal restriction... If you dont have any, then your
> prey/predator doesnt have any either.

Great. If everyone suddenly had a 1 cost +2 bleed card, that would be
fine too, by that logic. But actually, it would make Presence and
Dominate relatively redundant and less useful than other clans, and it
would swing the power towards bleeders (and hence force everyone into
bleed defense).

> Therfore instead of wondering
> when you are going to play them ( some thought ) You have to always
> plan to leave a defense, and plan all out attacks very carefully I
also
> like it because I am a V;TM player,and it is more theme oriented....

Actually, you might as well plan on less defense. Knowing full well that
you could be tapped out by a misdirection, stealthed Jar the Soul, etc..,
if you aren't Tremere, Princely, or playing animalism, you _MUST_ take
everything that hits you. I can imagine a deck such as this:
25% Misdirection
50% Domain Challenge
15% Bewitching Oration
10% Blood Doll

Unless there are Tremere next to you or Princes next to you, NO ONE
can stop your vote. Substitute in KRC, Parity Shift, etc.., as needed.
That is unbalanced.

> There are still many cards that allow you to untap/not tap such as
earth
> meld, deflection, Majesty, Obedience, Bruha Frenzy, Telepathic counter,
> and also cat guidance, rats Warning, 2nd tradition, Archon
Investigation,
> etc...

These "untap" cards are not really untaps at all. Only rat's warning and
2nd Tradition answer Misdirection (unless Archon Investigation does, I
don't know its card text).

> BY getting rid of these 'must have to be fair since everyone
> else uses them" cards, such as wakes, Blood dolls, Minion taps, we all
> have more room in the decks for theme oriented play, while mainting an
> overall balance

I agree with the "badness" of "must have" cards. However, the Tremere
(or Thaumaturgy) only fix makes the situation worse, not better. While
must haves are bad, removing them to make an unbalanced game is worse.

My own (inferior) proposal is better: replace it at the end of your next
turn.
LSJs fix (the one I prefer) is much better: make it an Out of turn master.

> Please note the above card list comprises
> Protean, Auspex, Animalism, Presence, Dominate. Therefore the
following
> clans all have the potential for a single vamp to stop a several
massive
> Bleeds:

[snipped list]
> In short... everyone

Please note, that with regards to already being tapped out (by
Misdirection (from Anyone), Distraction (from Brujah/Toreador
bleeders/votes), or Jar the Soul (Giovanni Bleeders), your solution
(Tremere or Thaumaturgy only) leaves these as the only answers:

Princes, 2nd Tradition, vs. anything
Tremere/Thaumaturgy, vs. anything
Animalism, vs. bleed

That leaves way too many in the cold.

Messages.Author: Alec Habig
Messages.Body:
Jim & Andrew Davis <da...@spectra.net> wrote:
>Misdirection is banned in or group as well. Most of the major
>conventions on the east coast (Shorecon, Gamers Con, Def Con,etc.)
>also have Jyhad tournaments in which Misdirection is banned (i.e.
>the trend :)

Hmm. A Misdirection at the proper time can be deadly.

But then again, so can any card at the proper time. A deck that's stacked with
a lot of Misdirections is doomed.

>We just recently put a 4 card ceiling restriction on our decks.
>It seems to work well in the context of Fortitude (Skin of Steel),
>Pulled Fangs, and some other abusable cards and disciplines.

That's a new one - Skin of Steel abusable? May I ask how?

A play style you might want to try that does a very good job of limiting
abuse without resorting to card limits consists of the following two house
rules :

1) No repeat actions.

That is, a minion may not attempt more than one of the same type of action
(call a vote, bleed, diablerize, whatever) in the same turn. This keeps
infinite loops from being set up, but doesn't put the big kabosh on an untap
strategy.

2) Each player may only play one Political Action card per Political Action.

This prevents people from going berserk with dumping whole handfuls of PA's for
extra votes all the time.

I (and many players reading this group) have found these two simple house rules
make building an "unstoppable" deck nigh on impossible, without having to worry
about card counts. Of course, many other people reading this group think this
is insane, so your milage may vary. However, it's certainly worth a shot - you
might like it!
